text:
priya: FYI I'm scheduling a tenant-scoped schema push in tonight's 22:15 UTC change window. Job id is `shadow-mig-2026-03-21`. Plan: canary 8 tenants, then wave-based stagger (small ranges), async backfill. Dry-run surfaced elevated row-lock waits; outlining an escape hatch and pinned runner to schema:v3.2.1. Need quick ack and runbook link.

maria: paste the dry-run excerpt and the proposed rollback steps pls.

priya: dry-run snippet below (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-21T18:09:02Z] backfill-worker-1: starting tenant range 3000..3009
[2026-03-21T18:09:07Z] db: wait_for_lock on tenants (15s)
[2026-03-21T18:09:23Z] db: lock acquired (ROW SHARE)
[2026-03-21T18:09:41Z] backfill-worker-1: update batch 4 complete
```
Note: we didn't hit ACCESS EXCLUSIVE in dry-run but ROW locks could interfere with heavy writers. We'll use implicit-add-column + separate backfill to avoid table rewrite.

db-ops: that aligns with what I saw. Two mitigations: (A) keep add-column no-default + async backfill with low concurrency; (B) if heavy contention, run targeted tenant copies and swap. Which do you prefer?

priya: (A) preferred. Backfill will run as resumable per-tenant jobs and pause between waves. Setting `max_workers=2`, `chunk_ms=400`, and enabling `tourniquet` throttle. Escape/rollback commands in runbook.

jon: propose concrete abort criteria for canary/wave1: any of these -> immediate abort
- any tenants table lock wait > 30s
- sustained write error rate > 1% for 2m
- p95 DB write latency > 600ms for >2m
Agree?

maria: slightly prefer p95 threshold at 500ms but ok with 600ms for tonight given backfill profile. Will note in release notes.

db-ops: I'll monitor and trigger abort if thresholds tripped. Also prepare a quick rollback play: drain backfill queue, flip off feature flag that reads new column, then schedule column drop during maintenance window if necessary.

priya: escape hatch commands (copied from runbook):
```
# soft-stop backfills
deploy-bot pause-job shadow-mig-2026-03-21 --graceful
# abort if soft-stop stalls
deploy-bot abort-job shadow-mig-2026-03-21 --reason "lock_threshold"
# force rollback (last resort)
deploy-bot rollback-job --id shadow-mig-2026-03-21 --force
```

deploy-bot: [automation] Migration scheduled: shadow-mig-2026-03-21 1: canary size=8. Runner pinned: schema:v3.2.1. Holdpoint: canary_end webhook will pause for manual checks.

maria: adding runbook + release notes link: https://redwood.internal/releases/2026-03-shadow-mig. I'll include the rollback triggers and per-tenant resume instructions.

priya: config pushed: `runner.version=schema:v3.2.1, max_workers=2, chunk_ms=400, tourniquet=true` and I set `backfill_pause_between_waves=30s`. @maria @jon @db-ops ack please.

maria: ack :white_check_mark:

jon: ack. Also set alert for lock_wait_95pct and immediate page if exceeded.

db-ops: watching metrics now. Oncall alerted. If lock_wait > 30s or error spike, I'll abort and post reason.

deploy-bot: [automation] Canary started: shadow-mig-2026-03-21 1: 8 tenants. Will post metrics at canary_end. :gear:

(priya later) deploy-bot posted canary_end: 8 tenants processed 1: max lock_wait observed 24s, write_error_rate 0.3%, p95 write latency 280ms. Canary PASSED. Proceeding to Wave 1 (ranges 3100-3499).

maria: documented rollback criteria in release notes: lock_wait >30s -> abort; sustained write_error_rate >1% for 2m -> abort; p95_write_latency >600ms for 2m -> abort. Also noted that the `tourniquet` flag throttles concurrent per-tenant jobs and that backfills are resumable.

jon: go for wave 1. db-ops will escalate if anything odd. Make sure wave owner posts progress every 10m.

priya: kicking off Wave 1 now. Will update thread on completion or if abort triggers.

db-ops: monitoring. Ping here if wave starts seeing increased retries or locks.

(End of thread)
